title: KPT step 3: two special k changes
summary: Treat k → j and k → v as small, separately memorised word families.
objectives: Recognise k → j in supplied word pairs.
Recognise k → v in supplied word pairs.
Avoid guessing these changes for unfamiliar words.

sections.title: Learn the pair with the word
paragraphs: Some k changes are less predictable for a beginner. Learn each supplied dictionary form together with its weak partner.
This block contains only k → j and k → v.

sections.title: Recognition before free production
paragraphs: Read both forms aloud or silently and point to the changed position.
The later mixed block will ask you to distinguish these from the earlier KPT families.

steps: The supplied forms show k becoming j.
Keep oi in poika and oj in pojan as one learned pair.
The final -n is separate from KPT.
The supplied forms show k becoming v.
Do not apply this change to every word containing k.

commonMistakes: Do not assume every k becomes j.
Do not assume every k becomes v.
Use only the supplied and practised word families at this level.

practiceExercises.prompt: What changes in poika (“boy”) → pojan (“of the boy”)?
practiceExercises.explanation: In this learned pair, k becomes j.

optionFeedback.k → j: Correct. In this learned pair, k becomes j.
optionFeedback.k → v: “k → v” does not show the required pattern. In this learned pair, k becomes j.
optionFeedback.k → ∅: “k → ∅” does not show the required pattern. In this learned pair, k becomes j.

practiceExercises.prompt: What changes in puku (“suit”) → puvun (“of the suit”)?
practiceExercises.explanation: In this learned pair, k becomes v.

optionFeedback.k → v: Correct. In this learned pair, k becomes v.
optionFeedback.k → j: “k → j” does not show the required pattern. In this learned pair, k becomes v.
optionFeedback.p → v: “p → v” does not show the required pattern. In this learned pair, k becomes v.

practiceExercises.prompt: Practice only: aika (“time”) → ____ (“of the time”) · use supplied genitive -n; apply k → j
practiceExercises.explanation: Use the learned weak partner aja- and the displayed complete form ajan.

practiceExercises.prompt: Practice only: luku (“number or chapter”) → ____ (“of the number or chapter”) · use supplied genitive -n; apply k → v
practiceExercises.explanation: Use the learned weak partner luvu- and the displayed complete form luvun.
